summary: The Board of Equalization is a five-member elected tax board. Since lawmakers stripped most of its duties in 2017, it advises county assessors, sets the taxable value of utility and railroad property, and hears some taxpayer appeals. District 2 covers much of Northern California's coast and the Bay Area, including Santa Clara County. Two Democrats advanced: incumbent Sally Lieber, elected in 2022, placed first in the June 2 primary with 56.8%, and John Pimentel, a San Mateo County Community College District trustee, placed second with 15.8%.

positions.stance: Defends the board's role and emphasizes hands-on tax-administration experience. She chairs the board for 2026. (Factually summaries of local coverage; Wikipedia)
Believes the board could be reformed or abolished, with its remaining work folded into other tax agencies. (GrowSF; Redwood City Pulse)
Would push to eliminate the sales tax on food and close 'unfair tax loopholes'. (Ballotpedia candidate survey)

key_differences: Pimentel is open to abolishing the board. Lieber defends it.

Both were reported in May and June 2026 to be largely self-funding. Lieber had raised about $225,000, about $200,500 of it her own money, and Pimentel about $258,000, $250,000 of it his own. Those figures are early and come from a secondary source.
Pimentel's endorsements cross the usual lines. They include the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and the San Francisco Chronicle editorial board.
